methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $5.7B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 1 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 2 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The Boring Company, a Series G transportation infrastructure venture, was last valued at $5.7B post-money and has raised $908M to date. The comparable universe in transportation is sparse: two private peers (Rivian and Einride) exist, though neither provides sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage data to support a reliable peer-median approach. No public comparables in the narrow transportation infrastructure category are available.

Given the limited peer set, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Applying a 1.25x multiplier typical for Series G progression to the $5.7B last post-money valuation yields $7.1B. This represents the median point in a range anchored at $6.1B (low) and $8.2B (high), derived from sensitivity analysis around the step-up assumption.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B to $8.2B, with $7.1B as the central case. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of comparable transaction data at this stage and valuation tier in the sector. The range reflects variance around stage-progression assumptions rather than empirical peer validation. Any refinement would require either closer transportation infrastructure comps at advanced stages or evidence supporting alternative step-up multiples for Series G rounds.
